venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner’s run family, how the line leads it, and why White’s safeties being deep left the short throw open.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — film session from full SEC broadcast. Fan rail empty until Charles approves.
headline: Same run. Different man leading. Two safeties deep.

offense.body:
He has a base run. All five linemen step the same way. They put two on a tackle, then one of them goes up to the linebacker. The back picks the hole. That is most of the night.

He will also start under center and stretch you to the sideline. The line steps sideways. The back runs sideways until a seam opens, then he cuts up. That was the first Florida run of the game. About nine yards.

He will send a guard the other way. You flow with the line, the guard is already leading the back behind you.

Third-and-2 in the third quarter, he did the long-run version. The tight end pinned their end inside. The left tackle ran around him and led Baugh. Baugh pressed the edge, followed that tackle, and was gone. That is the 61.

He will send an extra man across after the snap so the backside end gets kicked out. He will leave an end unblocked on purpose. If that end crashes on Baugh, Philo keeps it.

He moves a receiver before the snap to see if you follow him. If you follow, it is man. If you stay, it is zone. The next play is built off that.

The throws are off those runs. Fake the run, roll the other way, tight end in the flat. Fake the run, linebackers step up, throw the tight end where they just left. Or throw it now and let the tackles get out in front. Stockton’s first-quarter score is that screen.

When the corner is sitting eight yards off, he throws the hitch and the out. When they put extra men on Baugh, he throws it over the top. Abrams. Sixty-three yards.

Pistol showed up once. One look. Not the offense.

The twenty-yard loss inside the five is the snap, not a block. Moore. Philo ran it himself once, their end was still there, lost two. Idea was the keep. Play lost.
bullets: Creep up for Baugh and Brown scores from 49.
Follow the fake and the ball goes the other way.
Stay put and Baugh rips off 61 when everybody knew.

defense.body:
He plays four down linemen and an extra defensive back for their third receiver. Two linebackers. Two safeties standing 12 to 15 yards deep. The corners start 7 to 8 yards off the receiver.

That is a choice. Nothing deep gets started. The short throw is open. That is why FAU ran 90 plays. Henry and Valsin lived on the five-to-eight yard catch. Sumrall said it: third-and-1, you cannot have your corner nine yards off. That happened.

They rush four most snaps. They will walk the linebackers up into the gaps so it looks like a blitz, then those linebackers drop. That is fake pressure. The real extra rusher shows up on short yardage — a defensive back off the edge. They also twist two interior linemen so a tackle comes free.

In the red zone the safeties come down to about eight yards and the box gets heavy. They stuffed the inside run at the 1 more than once. They still lost the yard.

What they win on tape: Chiles and Coleman see the screen and kill it. The four-man rush gets home. Coleman sells the middle, Veltkamp thinks the sideline is one-on-one, Coleman is over the top and intercepts it at Florida’s 5.

FAU never huddles. Shotgun. Inside run and the five-to-eight yard throw. Veltkamp runs it when the edge leaves.
bullets: The short throw stayed open. Ninety plays.
White moves Woods so the tackle never settles.
Coleman sells the middle, then intercepts it at Florida’s 5.

specials.body: Durkin from 53. Clean. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt starts Florida’s second score.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt starts Florida’s second score.

nextWeek.look: They will throw it short and the quarterback will run it. Sixkiller is their guy. Hand it to Baugh. Ask a new question. Stand on the short throw. Keep Woods on the outside when Sixkiller runs it.
